Ormat Technologies develops, owns and operates geothermal and recovered-energy power plants and manufactures the related power equipment. It sells electricity under long-term contracts to utilities, runs a product segment selling turbines and systems, and has an energy storage and solar business. Based in Reno, Nevada, it operates mainly in the United States, Kenya, Guatemala, Indonesia and New Zealand, with roughly 1,800 employees and about 1.2 GW of capacity. Listed on the NYSE (ORA). B2B utility supplier with very low consumer brand visibility.

Perpetua Resources is a development-stage mining company building the Stibnite Gold Project in central Idaho, which would produce gold and antimony, a critical mineral used in batteries, flame retardants and munitions. It has no revenue yet and is funded by equity raises and government-linked financing including US Export-Import Bank and Department of Defense support. Based in Donnelly, Idaho; listed on Nasdaq and the TSX (PPTA). Exploration and development stage, B2B, minimal consumer brand awareness; mainly relevant for local and government-affairs visibility.

QTS Thunder Managing Issuer, LLC is a financing subsidiary linked to QTS Data Centers, the large US data centre operator owned by Blackstone since 2021. Such issuer vehicles raise asset-backed or securitized debt secured by data centre assets, which explains the multi-billion funding total shown. Located in Overland Park, Kansas, where QTS is headquartered. It is a special-purpose finance entity, not an operating business with customers or brand of its own. No consumer visibility; not a realistic sponsorship prospect, though parent QTS may be. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Rongsheng Petrochemical is a major Chinese private petrochemical group, listed in Shenzhen (002493), built around the Zhejiang Petrochemical complex at Zhoushan, a 40 million tonne-per-year integrated refinery and chemicals site. It produces refined oil products, aromatics, olefins, polyester and plastics sold to industrial customers across China. Founded in 1995 and based in Hangzhou, it is among China's largest private chemical groups, with Saudi Aramco holding a minority stake in the Zhoushan venture. B2B commodity business with little consumer brand profile.

SEARAH is the name used for the joint venture of Italian energy major Eni and Malaysian state oil company PETRONAS, formed to combine their upstream oil and gas assets in Indonesia and Malaysia. The venture was announced in 2025 as a new independent regional gas and LNG-focused player, with roughly a combined production of several hundred thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day. Based in London. Owned by Eni and PETRONAS; B2B energy producer with low consumer visibility, although its parents are known sports sponsors. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Sound Physicians is a US physician services organization providing hospital-based medicine, including hospitalists, critical care, emergency medicine and transitions-of-care programs. It contracts with hospitals and health systems to staff and manage inpatient care, earning fees from hospital partners and professional billing. Founded in 2001 and based in Nashville, Tennessee (originally Tacoma, Washington), it works in hundreds of hospitals across many states with thousands of clinicians. Privately held, backed by Summit Partners and later Centerbridge and other investors. B2B healthcare staffing with limited public brand awareness.

Southern California Edison is the main electric utility for much of Southern California, a regulated subsidiary of Edison International (NYSE: EIX). It generates, buys and delivers electricity to roughly 15 million people across about 50,000 square miles, serving some 5 million customer accounts, and invests heavily in grid hardening against wildfire risk and in clean energy. Headquartered in Rosemead, California, with around 14,000 employees and annual revenue above 15 billion dollars. Consumer-facing utility known locally by every household in its territory but not a global brand; already active in community sponsorships.

Target is a large American general-merchandise retailer operating about 1,950 stores plus a major online and same-day pickup business. It sells groceries, apparel, home goods, electronics and toys, including strong owned brands such as Good & Gather, Cat & Jack and Threshold, and runs the Target Circle loyalty programme. Headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, founded in 1902 with the Target format launched in 1962; roughly 400,000 employees and about 105 billion dollars in revenue. Listed on the NYSE (TGT). Highly visible US consumer brand with little presence outside the United States.

Transurban is an Australian toll road operator that owns and manages urban motorways in Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane and the Greater Washington area in the United States, and also holds a stake in the Montreal A25. Revenue comes from tolls paid by motorists and commercial vehicle operators under long-term concessions. Headquartered in Melbourne, Victoria, and listed on the ASX (TCL) with a market value of around 40 billion Australian dollars. It operates CityLink in Melbourne and the 495 Express Lanes in Virginia. Known to motorists locally but a B2C-adjacent infrastructure brand, not widely recognized abroad.

United Rentals is the largest equipment rental company in the world, with more than 1,500 branches across North America and Europe. It rents construction, industrial and specialty equipment such as aerial lifts, excavators, power and temperature control, trench safety and fluid solutions to contractors, manufacturers, utilities, events and government customers, and also sells used equipment. Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, with roughly 26,000 employees and about 15 billion dollars in annual revenue. Listed on the NYSE (URI). Strong B2B brand within construction and industry, little consumer awareness.

Vale is a Brazilian mining company and one of the world's largest producers of iron ore and iron ore pellets, plus nickel, copper and other base metals, serving steelmakers and industrial customers mainly in China, Asia and Europe. Headquartered in Rio de Janeiro, with major operations in Carajas and Minas Gerais and mines in Canada. Founded in 1942 as state-owned Companhia Vale do Rio Doce and privatized in 1997. Listed on the Sao Paulo exchange (VALE3) and the NYSE (VALE). B2B commodity producer with strong Brazilian brand recognition and a history of sports sponsorship in Brazil.

Vedanta Resources is the London-based holding company of Indian natural resources conglomerate Vedanta Limited, controlled by Anil Agarwal. Its subsidiaries produce zinc, lead, silver, aluminium, copper, iron ore, oil and gas, and power, and are building businesses in steel and electronics; Hindustan Zinc and Cairn Oil & Gas are well known. The group operates mainly in India, with additional assets in South Africa and Namibia, and has carried significant debt that it restructured in recent years. Delisted from the London Stock Exchange in 2018. B2B commodities with modest consumer awareness outside India.

Waste Connections is a North American integrated solid waste services company, collecting, transferring, recycling and disposing of non-hazardous waste for residential, commercial and industrial customers, and operating landfills and energy exploration waste treatment. It focuses on secondary and rural markets across the US and Canada, with operations in about 45 states and six Canadian provinces. Revenue is around 9 billion dollars and employees about 24,000. Founded in 1997 and now headquartered in The Woodlands (Spring), Texas; listed on the NYSE and TSX (WCN). Local service brand, B2B and municipal, little national consumer visibility.

Whirlpool is one of the world's largest home appliance makers, producing washers, dryers, refrigerators, dishwashers, ovens and small appliances under brands including Whirlpool, KitchenAid, Maytag, Amana, JennAir, Indesit and Bauknecht. It sells through retailers, builders and online to consumers in nearly every region, with roughly 40,000 employees and about 16 billion dollars in revenue. Founded in 1911 and headquartered in Benton Harbor, Michigan. Listed on the NYSE (WHR). Very high consumer brand visibility, especially in North America, and a long record of marketing partnerships.

Zijin Mining is China's largest gold and copper miner, with operations in China and around 15 other countries including Serbia, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Tibet, Papua New Guinea and Suriname. It produces gold, copper, zinc, lithium and silver, and is expanding in lithium. Headquartered in Xiamen, Fujian, founded in 1993; listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (601899) and Hong Kong (2899). Revenue is above 40 billion dollars with tens of thousands of employees. Chinese state-linked ownership via Minxi Xinghang. B2B commodity producer with limited consumer brand awareness outside China.

Sotera Health is a provider of sterilization and lab testing services for the medical device, pharmaceutical and food safety industries, operating through Sterigenics (contract sterilization, ethylene oxide, gamma and e-beam), Nordion (cobalt-60 isotopes) and Nelson Labs (testing). Customers include major medtech and pharma manufacturers. Headquartered in Broadview Heights, Ohio, with facilities worldwide and about 3,000 employees; revenue roughly 1 billion dollars. IPO on Nasdaq in 2020 (SHC), majority held by Warburg Pincus and GTCR. B2B healthcare services with no consumer brand profile and ongoing ethylene oxide litigation.

Air Products and Chemicals is a leading supplier of industrial gases such as oxygen, nitrogen, argon and hydrogen, along with related equipment and services, to refining, chemicals, metals, electronics, food and healthcare customers. It is a major builder of large hydrogen and clean energy projects, including NEOM in Saudi Arabia. Founded in 1940 and headquartered in Allentown, Pennsylvania, with operations in over 50 countries, roughly 23,000 employees and about 12 billion dollars of revenue. Listed on the NYSE (APD). B2B with low consumer awareness.

Albemarle is a specialty chemicals company and one of the world's largest producers of lithium for electric vehicle batteries, plus bromine specialties for flame retardants and catalysts for refining. Customers are battery makers, automakers, electronics firms and refiners. Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, with major lithium operations in Chile (Atacama), Australia and the US; revenue has swung between roughly 3.5 and 7 billion dollars with lithium prices. Listed on the NYSE (ALB). B2B materials supplier with limited consumer brand visibility.

Ardagh Group is a global manufacturer of metal and glass packaging, supplying beverage cans, glass bottles and jars to drinks and food brands. Customers include major brewers, soft drink companies, wine and spirits makers and food producers across Europe, North America and Brazil. Headquartered in Luxembourg and controlled by the Paul Coulson family, it split into Ardagh Glass Packaging and Ardagh Metal Packaging (NYSE: AMBP). Revenue is around 9 billion dollars with about 23,000 employees. B2B supplier whose products are well known on shelves but whose name has little consumer recognition.

Atos is a French multinational IT services and digital transformation company, offering consulting, cybersecurity, cloud, managed infrastructure, data centre and big data and supercomputing (Eviden) solutions to enterprises and governments. Headquartered in Bezons near Paris, with around 100,000 employees and revenue of roughly 10 billion euros. Listed on Euronext Paris (ATO). Atos went through a major financial restructuring in 2024 and has been selling units. It has long been a major IT partner of the Olympic and Paralympic Games. Mostly B2B brand with sports-partnership experience.

HKC Corporation is a Chinese manufacturer of liquid crystal display panels and monitors for televisions, notebooks, tablets and smartphones, with large fab facilities in Chongqing, Changsha, Mianyang and other locations, plus its own HKC-branded consumer monitors. Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Shenzhen, Guangdong. It sells to global brand customers such as TV and PC makers and to consumers via monitors in China and abroad. It pursued a listing in Shenzhen. Scale is large in panels, but the HKC brand is mainly known in gaming monitors.

Motorola Solutions provides mission-critical communications and public safety technology: land mobile radios, body cameras, video security (Avigilon), command centre software and emergency call handling for police, fire, ambulance and enterprises. It was formed in 2011 when Motorola Inc. split into Motorola Solutions and Motorola Mobility. Headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, with about 21,000 employees and roughly 10 billion dollars in revenue. Listed on the NYSE (MSI). Customers are governments and enterprises worldwide. The Motorola name is widely known; the company has sports partnerships including security and communications services.

Multi-Color Corporation is a global manufacturer of label solutions for consumer brands in home and personal care, food and beverage, wine and spirits, healthcare and specialty sectors, making pressure-sensitive, in-mould, shrink sleeve and cut-and-stack labels. It operates dozens of plants across North America, Europe, Latin America, Asia and Australia. Based in Atlanta, Georgia, it was taken private by Clayton, Dubilier & Rice in 2019 after being listed on Nasdaq (LABL). B2B packaging supplier whose labels appear on well-known products but whose name has no consumer visibility.

Seahawk Holdings is a holding company with a base in Calgary, Alberta, Canada. The Crunchbase entry classifies it under information services and says it operates as a parent company that holds other businesses, with a multi-billion funding total shown. The available information does not state which subsidiaries it holds, who its customers are, or whether it is listed. Treat it as an investment or holding vehicle rather than a consumer-facing business. No known consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

VerSe Innovation is an Indian regional-language mobile content and technology company, running Dailyhunt (a news and content aggregator in more than a dozen Indian languages) and Josh (a short-video app launched after the TikTok ban in India). It earns revenue from advertising and brand partnerships and serves tens or hundreds of millions of monthly users. Headquartered in Bangalore, Karnataka, founded in 2007 as Eterno Infotech, backed by Google, Microsoft, Qatar Investment Authority, Goldman Sachs and others, with funding of around 1.7 billion dollars. Strong India consumer app brand and a youth audience.

Arkema is a French specialty chemicals and advanced materials group created in 2004 from the spin-off of Total's chemicals arm. It makes high-performance polymers (Kynar, Pebax), adhesives (Bostik), coating solutions, acrylics and intermediates for construction, batteries, packaging, transport and electronics. Headquartered in Colombes/Puteaux near Paris, with about 21,000 employees, sites in around 55 countries and revenue near 9 billion euros. Listed on Euronext Paris (AKE). B2B with low consumer awareness; Bostik adhesives and Pebax sports materials give some indirect visibility.

Avery Dennison is a materials science company making pressure-sensitive labels and packaging materials, RFID and digital identification solutions (used widely in apparel tracking), and graphics and reflective products. Customers are consumer goods, apparel, retail, logistics and healthcare firms. Founded in 1935 and headquartered in Mentor, Ohio (moving to Glendale, California), with about 35,000 employees in over 50 countries and revenue near 9 billion dollars. Listed on the NYSE (AVY). The Avery office-product brand was sold to CCL in 2014. B2B with strong industry presence, little consumer awareness.

BrightView is the largest commercial landscaping services provider in the United States, offering landscape maintenance, tree care, snow and ice removal and landscape development to corporate campuses, HOAs, hospitals, hotels, resorts, public parks and other commercial properties. Revenue is roughly 2.7 billion dollars with about 20,000 employees. Headquartered in Blue Bell, Pennsylvania, it was formed from Brickman and ValleyCrest, owned by KKR, and listed on the NYSE (BV) since 2018. B2B services brand with no consumer recognition outside property managers.

ContextLogic is the company behind Wish, the mobile shopping marketplace that sold low-priced goods, often shipped from China, directly to consumers. It listed on Nasdaq in 2020 (WISH), but sales collapsed, and in 2024 it sold the Wish platform to Qoo10 (Singapore) for 173 million dollars and became a shell company with cash and tax assets. Headquartered in Oakland, California, previously San Francisco, founded 2010 by Peter Szulczewski and Danny Zhang. Funding of about 1.6 billion dollars. Wish was a well-known mobile shopping app but is no longer an operating company.

Currenta is a German chemical park operator and service provider, running the CHEMPARKs at Leverkusen, Dormagen and Krefeld-Uerdingen in North Rhine-Westphalia. It supplies energy, utilities, waste management, analytics, safety, security and infrastructure to the chemical companies on those sites such as Bayer, Covestro and Lanxess. Headquartered in Leverkusen, it was created in 2007 as a Bayer and Lanxess joint venture; since 2019 it has been owned by Macquarie Asset Management. About 3,300 employees. B2B industrial services brand, little public profile.

Digital Currency Group (DCG) is a New York-area holding company for crypto businesses, founded in 2015 by Barry Silbert. Its portfolio has included Grayscale Investments (the Bitcoin Trust and other crypto funds), Genesis (lending, which went bankrupt in 2023), Foundry (mining services), Luno (exchange) and CoinDesk (sold in 2023), plus stakes in hundreds of startups. Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut. Privately held and a major crypto investor, it faced regulatory and legal issues after the Genesis collapse. Known within crypto circles; little mass consumer awareness.

DXP Enterprises is a Houston-based distributor and service provider of maintenance, repair and operating products, including pumps, bearings, seals, safety supplies and rotating equipment, along with supply chain services and integrated pump and water systems. It serves oil and gas, chemical, food and beverage, construction and general industrial customers across the US and Canada, with revenue of roughly 1.8 billion dollars. Founded in 1908 and listed on Nasdaq (DXPE). B2B industrial distribution brand with no consumer visibility.

EasyJet is a British low-cost airline founded in 1995 by Stelios Haji-Ioannou and headquartered at London Luton Airport. It operates a fleet of around 350 Airbus A320 family aircraft to over 150 airports in more than 35 countries, carrying roughly 90 million passengers a year, and sells package holidays via easyJet holidays. Revenue is about 9 billion pounds. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (EZJ) and FTSE 100 member. A well-known European consumer brand with high retail awareness.

Ensign Energy Services is a Canadian oilfield services company that provides contract land drilling, well servicing, directional drilling, rental equipment and related services to oil and gas producers. It operates a large fleet of land drilling rigs in Canada, the United States and internationally, including Australia and Latin America. Founded in 1987 and headquartered in Calgary, Alberta; listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (ESI). Revenue is roughly 1.5 to 2 billion Canadian dollars. B2B energy services with no consumer brand awareness.

Japan Tobacco (JT Group) is one of the world's largest tobacco companies, selling Winston, Camel (outside the US), Mevius and Ploom heated tobacco products in over 130 markets, after buying Gallaher in 2007. It also has pharmaceutical (Torii) and processed food businesses. Headquartered in Tokyo with around 50,000 employees and revenue exceeding 3 trillion yen. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (2914), with the Japanese government holding about a third. Tobacco brands are heavily restricted in advertising, which limits sponsorship relevance, although JT has a history in motorsport.

Klaviyo is a Boston-based marketing automation platform that helps e-commerce and consumer brands send email, SMS and push messages using customer data from stores such as Shopify. It earns subscription revenue from over 150,000 customers; ARR passed 1 billion dollars. Founded in 2012 by Andrew Bialecki and Ed Hallen. Listed on the NYSE (KVYO) since its September 2023 IPO. B2B software brand, well known among online merchants and marketers, little general consumer visibility.

MidCap Financial is a middle-market-focused specialty finance firm that originates and invests in senior secured loans to private-equity-backed companies, and is an affiliate of Apollo Global Management. It manages billions of dollars through MidCap Financial Investment Corporation (formerly Apollo Investment Corp, Nasdaq: MFIC) and private vehicles. Headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland, with offices in New York and London. B2B lender; no consumer awareness, though the Apollo parent is a well-known financial name.

Netomnia is a UK fibre broadband network operator (altnet) that builds full-fibre FTTP networks, largely in smaller towns and cities across Britain, and sells retail broadband under the YouFibre brand and wholesale access to other providers. It was founded in 2017 by Matthew Hare, who earlier founded Gigaclear, and has passed well over a million premises. Based in London, it is funded by private equity and debt financing from investors including Goldman Sachs Asset Management. Regional consumer brand with growing but limited national awareness.

NYDIG (New York Digital Investment Group) is a bitcoin-focused financial firm offering institutional custody, trading, lending, mining and bitcoin-enabled banking services, and managing funds. It enables community banks and fintechs to offer bitcoin to their customers. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York, it is majority owned by Stone Ridge Holdings, with strategic investment from banks and financial partners such as Mass Mutual, Soros Fund Management and Bessemer. B2B and institutional-facing; modest public brand awareness outside finance and crypto circles.

Publicis Groupe is one of the world's three largest advertising and communications holding companies, headquartered in Paris. Its agencies and platforms include Leo Burnett, Saatchi & Saatchi, Publicis Worldwide, Starcom, Zenith, Digitas, Razorfish, Epsilon and Sapient, and it acquired data firm Epsilon in 2019. Revenue is around 16 billion euros with about 100,000 employees in 100 countries. Listed on Euronext Paris (PUB). Customers are large global advertisers. B2B agency network; Leo Burnett and Saatchi are recognized in the industry but the group has low public awareness.

Sitecore is a digital experience platform and customer experience management software company. Its products cover web content management, personalization, commerce, customer data and marketing automation for large enterprises. Founded in Denmark in 2001 and now with executive offices in the US, it is backed by EQT since 2016 and serves thousands of customers worldwide. Funding shown suggests private equity financing, with EQT as the lead owner. B2B enterprise software brand with limited consumer visibility.

Steinhoff Africa Retail was the retail arm of the Steinhoff group, listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in 2017 and renamed Pepkor Holdings (JSE: PPH) in 2018. Its brands include Pep and Ackermans (value clothing and homeware), PEP Home, JD Group furniture banners such as Russells and Bradlows, and Tiger Wheel & Tyre. It serves value-oriented shoppers across South Africa and neighbouring countries through thousands of stores. Strong brand awareness in Southern Africa, particularly among lower-income households.

Syensqo is a Belgian advanced materials and specialty chemicals company spun off from Solvay in December 2023 (Solvay retained the commodities side). It makes high-performance polymers, composites, battery materials, aroma and fragrance ingredients and solvents for aerospace, automotive, electronics, energy and consumer goods. Headquartered in Brussels, with about 13,000 employees and sales near 6 billion euros. Listed on Euronext Brussels (SYENS). B2B with limited consumer awareness, although materials appear in aircraft and car components, and it has supported solar flight projects.

TMON (Ticket Monster) is a South Korean e-commerce platform that began as a daily-deal site and sells tickets, travel, local services and general merchandise to consumers through its app and website. Headquartered in Seoul, it was previously owned by LivingSocial and Groupon, and later by KKR and Anchor Equity Partners. In 2022 it was acquired by Qoo10 owner Qoo Group (Singapore), and in 2024 it was caught up in the TMON and WeMakePrice settlement-delay crisis and entered court receivership. Known Korean consumer brand with troubled finances.

Unisys is an American IT services and solutions company with legacy mainframe heritage. It provides digital workplace services, cloud and infrastructure, application services and ClearPath Forward mainframe software to governments and enterprises, including airlines, banks and public sector clients. Founded through the 1986 merger of Sperry and Burroughs, it is headquartered in Blue Bell, Pennsylvania, with roughly 16,000 employees and revenue about 2 billion dollars. Listed on the NYSE (UIS). B2B technology services brand with little consumer awareness.

Vivint is a US smart home technology company selling professionally installed security systems, cameras, doorbell cameras, automation and solar energy services under subscription contracts, through direct-to-home sales teams. It was founded in 1999 (as APX Alarm) and headquartered in Lehi, Utah. Blackstone acquired it in 2012, it listed through a SPAC in 2020 as Vivint Smart Home (NYSE: VVNT), and in 2023 NRG Energy acquired it for roughly 2.8 billion dollars. It serves about two million subscribers. Recognized US consumer brand, known for stadium naming partnerships such as the Utah Jazz arena.

Watco Companies is a Pittsburg, Kansas-based transportation and logistics company operating short-line and regional railroads, port terminals, transload and mechanical services. It runs dozens of short-line railroads across North America and Australia, handling agricultural, energy, chemicals and industrial freight, and offers terminal and shipping services. Privately held and family-run, founded in 1983 by Dick Webb. Revenue exceeds 1.5 billion dollars with several thousand employees. B2B logistics operator with little consumer brand visibility.

WeDoctor (Wedoctor Group, 微医) is a Chinese digital healthcare platform founded in 2010 in Hangzhou. It offers online appointment booking with hospitals, online consultations, internet hospitals, health insurance services and health management for patients and employers, and has worked with government health departments. Backed by Tencent, Alibaba affiliates and other investors, with funding of about 1.5 billion dollars. It filed for a Hong Kong IPO but did not complete it. Known consumer health app in China; no major overseas brand visibility.

Westlake Corporation is an American manufacturer of petrochemicals, polymers and building products, headquartered in Houston. Its Performance and Essential Materials segment makes PVC, caustic soda, ethylene and polyethylene, while Housing and Infrastructure Products includes siding, trim, pipe and fittings, windows and roofing under brands like Royal Building Products and North American Pipe. Controlled by the Chao family, listed on the NYSE (WLK) with revenue near 12 billion dollars and 16,000 employees. B2B industrial brand with building product recognition among contractors.

Aster Chemicals & Energy is a Singapore-based chemicals and energy company, formed from the former Shell petrochemicals assets in Singapore (Bukom and Jurong Island) which Shell sold in 2023 to a consortium of Chandra Asri Petrochemical (Indonesia) and Glencore. It operates a refinery and petrochemical plant including an ethylene cracker and related units, supplying fuels and chemicals regionally. The name was adopted in 2024 after the transfer. Its owners are Chandra Asri and Glencore. B2B with little consumer brand visibility.

Babytree is a Chinese parenting and maternal community platform that began as a forum in 2007 and grew into an app with content, social features and e-commerce for expectant and new parents. It earns revenue from advertising, online sales of baby products and health services. Headquartered in Beijing, it has tens of millions of monthly active users, and was backed by Tencent and other investors, with about 1 billion dollars of funding shown. It went public in Hong Kong (1761) and later its e-commerce Meitun business was a major part. Well-known mother-and-baby consumer brand in China.

Bitauto Holdings is a Chinese automotive internet services company running Yiche, an online platform for new and used car information, advertising and transaction services. It earns revenue from advertising by automakers and dealers and from a transaction services platform. Headquartered in Beijing, it was listed on the NYSE (BITA) from 2010, backed by Tencent, JD.com and Baidu, and in 2020 was taken private by a consortium that included Tencent and Hillhouse. Well-known auto portal in China, B2B2C in nature, with buying-intent audience.

CapitaLand is one of Asia's largest diversified real estate groups, headquartered in Singapore and owned by Temasek. It owns and manages shopping malls, offices, serviced residences, lodging and logistics and data centre properties across more than 200 cities in around 30 countries, and runs listed REITs and private funds. The group had about 130 billion Singapore dollars of assets under management. In 2021 it restructured into CapitaLand Investment (SGX: 9CI) and CapitaLand Development. Strong brand in Asian property and retail; mall brands are consumer-visible.

Chipone Technology is a Beijing-based Chinese integrated circuit design company, working on chips for display drivers and mobile devices, and related power and driver ICs. Its products serve Chinese smartphone and display panel manufacturers. Founded in 2008, it has listed on the Shanghai STAR Market in 2023 (688593). Funding of around 6.5 billion yuan is shown. B2B semiconductor supplier with no consumer brand visibility.

Cloudera is a data management and analytics software company, born from the Hadoop era. Its platform lets enterprises store, process and analyse data across clouds and data centres, with offerings for machine learning, data engineering and data warehousing, and it merged with Hortonworks in 2019. Headquartered in Santa Clara, California, it listed on the NYSE in 2017 and was taken private by KKR and Clayton, Dubilier & Rice in 2021 in a roughly 5.3 billion dollar deal. B2B enterprise software with no consumer visibility.

Club Med is a French all-inclusive holiday resort operator founded in 1950 by Gerard Blitz, known for beach and ski resorts around the world with sports, kids' clubs and dining included. It runs about 65-70 villages in dozens of countries and sells to families and couples, mostly European and Asian guests. Headquartered in Paris, it has been owned by Chinese conglomerate Fosun International since 2015 after being delisted from Euronext. Revenue is about 2 billion euros. Very well known consumer travel brand, particularly in France and China.

CSW Industrials is a diversified industrial growth company based in Dallas, Texas, making specialty chemicals, HVAC/R products, plumbing and electrical products, and building products. Brands include RectorSeal, Whitmore, Smoke Guard, Greco and Safe-T-Switch, sold through distributors to contractors and OEMs. It was spun off from Capital Southwestern in 2015, and is listed on Nasdaq (CSWI). Revenue is around 800 million dollars. B2B with brand recognition among trades, no mass consumer visibility.

Distribution Solutions Group is an industrial distribution company formed in 2022 through the merger of Lawson Products with TestEquity and Gexpro Services, backed by Luther King Capital Management. It distributes MRO supplies, test and measurement equipment and supply chain services for OEMs to industrial, aerospace, telecom and utility customers in North America and beyond. It is headquartered in Chicago and listed on Nasdaq (DSGR). Revenue is about 1.8 billion dollars. B2B industrial distributor with no consumer visibility.

e2open is a cloud-based supply chain software provider offering a connected platform for planning, logistics, trade compliance and sourcing across trading partners, based in Addison, Texas. It was created in 2021 when a SPAC (CC Neuberger Principal Holdings I) merged with e2open, and it listed on the NYSE (ETWO). In 2025 it was acquired by WiseTech Global in a deal valued around 2.1 billion dollars. Customers include large manufacturers, retailers and logistics providers. B2B software with no consumer visibility.

Forte is a San Francisco blockchain infrastructure company that built tools for game developers to add digital assets, tokens and economies to games. Founded in 2018, it was led by Josh Williams and raised hundreds of millions of dollars from backers including Griffin Gaming Partners and Andreessen Horowitz, with total funding of about 910 million dollars shown. It served game studios rather than players, so it is B2B with little consumer awareness. It cut staff during the crypto downturn.

Gett is a ride-hailing and corporate ground transportation platform, founded in Israel in 2010, that is best known for black cab bookings in London and business travel services. It earns commissions on rides and enterprise fees for corporate accounts, serving businesses, drivers and consumers in the UK, Israel and Europe. Headquartered in London, it merged with Juno and got backing from Volkswagen, Access Industries and others, raising over 900 million dollars. It left several markets and focused on B2B in Europe. Recognizable in London for black cab app use.

Hersha Hospitality Trust is a real estate investment trust that owned upscale and upper-midscale hotels in urban and gateway markets such as New York, Boston, Philadelphia, Washington DC and Miami, under franchise brands including Marriott, Hilton and Hyatt. Headquartered in Philadelphia, it was listed on the NYSE (HT) and was acquired in 2023 by KSL Capital Partners for about 1.4 billion dollars and taken private. Revenue came from room and food and beverage operations of its hotel portfolio. B2B owner with no direct consumer brand.

Innoscience is a Chinese manufacturer of gallium nitride power semiconductors, running an integrated device manufacturing model with an 8-inch GaN-on-silicon wafer fab in Suzhou and another in Zhuhai. Its chips serve electric vehicle, data centre, consumer fast-charger and LiDAR customers. Founded in 2015 in Zhuhai and now headquartered in Suzhou, Jiangsu, it raised more than 1 billion dollars from investors including CATL and SK Hynix and listed in Hong Kong (2577) in December 2024. B2B component supplier with no consumer visibility.

Legal & General is a British financial services company, one of the largest in the UK, providing life insurance, pensions, annuities, retirement solutions and asset management through Legal & General Investment Management. It also invests in housing and urban regeneration. Headquartered in London, founded in 1836, with roughly 12,000 employees and managing over 1 trillion pounds of assets. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (LGEN), FTSE 100. Well-known British consumer finance brand with the umbrella logo and a history of sponsorship in sport.

Lvmama is a Chinese online travel service provider (lvmama.com) offering domestic and outbound tours, attraction tickets, hotels and holiday packages to consumers through its website and app. Headquartered in Shanghai and founded in 2008, it was backed by investors including Fosun. Funding of around 980 million dollars is shown. It competed with Ctrip and Tuniu and its ownership has changed over time. Known in China among leisure travellers, with a mid-level brand profile.

Norfolk Southern Corporation is one of the largest US freight railroads, operating about 19,000 route miles in 22 states and Washington DC, and serving most major eastern ports. It carries intermodal, coal, automotive, chemicals, agricultural and industrial goods for shippers. Headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, it has around 20,000 employees and revenue of roughly 12 billion dollars. Listed on the NYSE (NSC). Union Pacific announced a plan to acquire it in 2025. Known for the 2023 East Palestine derailment. B2B transport brand with moderate public recognition in the eastern US.

Nova Chemicals is a Calgary-based producer of polyethylene and styrenic polymers, including performance polyethylene such as Sclair and Surpass resins used in flexible packaging, containers and films. It operates plants in Alberta, Ontario and Pennsylvania. It has been wholly owned by Mubadala Investment Company of Abu Dhabi since 2009 (formerly through International Petroleum Investment Company). Revenue is about 3 billion dollars annually. B2B petrochemical producer with little consumer awareness, though in Alberta it is a local sponsor.

Orbia is a Mexican-founded global group (formerly Mexichem) with operations across five business groups: Polymer Solutions, Building and Infrastructure (Wavin pipes), Precision Agriculture (Netafim drip irrigation), Connectivity Solutions and Fluor and Energy Materials (Koura refrigerants). It sells to construction, agriculture, telecom and healthcare customers in about 50 countries, with revenue near 7.5 billion dollars. Listed on the Mexican exchange (ORBIA), with a Boston business office. B2B industrial brand, some local awareness via Wavin and Netafim.

Outbrain is a New York-based advertising technology company known for content recommendation widgets (the 'Around the Web' links on publisher sites) and for its Teads acquisition in 2024. It earns revenue when advertisers pay to promote content or video across premium publishers and apps. Founded in 2006 in Israel, it listed on Nasdaq in 2021 (OB). After buying Teads, it renamed itself Teads Holding. Customers are brands, agencies and publishers. B2B ad-tech with limited consumer recognition.

Polaris Inc. is a manufacturer of off-road vehicles, snowmobiles, motorcycles and boats, with brands including Polaris RZR and Ranger, Indian Motorcycle, Slingshot, Ski-Doo competitors, Pontoon boats and Aixam. It sells through dealers worldwide to consumers and commercial customers, with revenue of about 7 billion dollars and 15,000 employees. Founded in 1954 in Roseau, Minnesota, and headquartered in Medina (Long Lake area), Minnesota. Listed on the NYSE (PII). Strong enthusiast consumer brand with extensive racing and event sponsorship experience.

Qunar.com is a major Chinese online travel platform and search engine for flights, hotels and tour packages, headquartered in Beijing and founded in 2005. Baidu owned a majority stake, and Qunar listed on Nasdaq in 2013 (QUNR) before merging with Ctrip (Trip.com Group) in 2015, with Ctrip taking a stake and Baidu receiving shares. After the Ctrip tie-up it was taken private. Customers are consumers and travel suppliers. Well-known Chinese travel brand with an active mobile app user base.

Red Star Macalline is a leading Chinese home furnishing mall operator, with over 300 large shopping malls and branded stores across China where furniture makers, brands and retailers lease space. Headquartered in Shanghai, founded in 1986 by Che Jianxin family and listed in Hong Kong (1528) and Shanghai (601828). It has expanded into e-commerce, home design and platform services. In 2023-24 it was acquired in part by Alibaba's Taobao and Tmall interests; control shifted to Yinhai Zhongnan. Recognized consumer brand across Chinese cities, with housing-market exposure.

Shiji Group is a hospitality and retail technology provider, supplying cloud software for hotels, restaurants and retailers, including property management, point-of-sale, distribution and guest-engagement systems. Customers include large global hotel chains. Founded in Beijing in 1998 and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (002153), it now has a Singapore base shown here and offices in more than 80 countries. B2B software provider with no consumer visibility.

Sunlight Financial is a US point-of-sale financing technology company that connected solar installers, contractors and lenders, letting homeowners finance residential solar and home improvements. It listed in 2021 through a SPAC merger with Spartan Acquisition Corp. III (NYSE: SUNL) at about 1.3 billion dollars. Based in Charlotte, North Carolina, it faced a drop in demand and impairments and filed for Chapter 11 in October 2023, emerging as a private company in 2024. B2B fintech with no consumer recognition.

Tanium is an endpoint management and security software company that gives IT and security teams real-time visibility and control of laptops, servers and devices on large networks, with products for asset discovery, patching, risk and compliance. Founded by David Hindawi and Orion Hindawi, it is headquartered in Kirkland/Bellevue, Washington, privately held and valued at around 9 billion dollars in 2020. Customers include large enterprises and government agencies, with funding of about 1 billion dollars. B2B cybersecurity brand with limited public consumer recognition.

Vantage Specialty Chemicals is a US producer of natural-based specialty ingredients, including oleochemicals, emollients and derivatives used in personal care, cosmetics, home care, and industrial and nutrition applications. Headquartered in Deerfield, Illinois, it was formed through a private equity-backed combination of chemical businesses and sells to consumer brands and formulators worldwide. Funding shown is about 900 million dollars. B2B ingredients supplier with no direct consumer brand profile.

Zymergen was a synthetic biology company in Emeryville, California that used robotics, machine learning and genetic engineering to design microbes that produce materials and chemicals. It raised about 970 million dollars from SoftBank and others and listed on Nasdaq in April 2021 (ZY) but its first product, Hyaline film, failed to meet customers' needs. Ginkgo Bioworks acquired it in 2022 for about 300 million dollars, and it was subsequently folded into Ginkgo. Small public profile and no longer an independent company.

Affin Bank is a Malaysian banking group, tracing back to 1975, providing retail, commercial, Islamic banking and investment banking services, plus asset management and insurance interests. It is headquartered in Kuala Lumpur and listed on Bursa Malaysia (AFFIN), with the Malaysian Armed Forces Fund Board as a major shareholder. It operates a branch network across Malaysia with a few thousand staff. Consumer-facing bank with moderate Malaysian brand awareness and a history of sponsorship of local sport and events.

AIWAYS is a Chinese electric vehicle maker headquartered in Shanghai, known for the U5 compact SUV and U6 coupe SUV, and it sells in Europe through a Munich-based European office. Founded in 2017, it is backed by Shanghai-based investors and Chinese auto partners. It sold limited volumes in Europe and went through financial difficulty, and it was reported to have produced vehicles with partners. Funding of about 5.2 billion yuan shown. Low consumer brand awareness in Europe.

Ampere Computing is a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2017 by Renee James, developing Arm-based server processors (Altra, AmpereOne) for cloud and data centre workloads. Customers include Oracle, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure and Tencent, and Ampere emphasizes power efficiency. Based in Santa Clara, California. Oracle held a significant stake, and in 2025 SoftBank agreed to acquire it for about 6.5 billion dollars. B2B chip designer with no consumer brand visibility.

Avaya is an enterprise communications company providing unified communications, contact centre software and cloud collaboration tools such as Avaya Experience Platform, serving large organisations, governments and call centres in over 100 countries. It was formed from Lucent's enterprise business in 2000, headquartered in Morristown, New Jersey (later Durham, NC), listed on the NYSE, and went through Chapter 11 bankruptcies in 2017 and 2023. It had about 5,000 employees post-restructuring. B2B brand with legacy telephone recognition; also a past sports sponsor.

Carzone (Chezhi) is a Shanghai-based Chinese auto parts e-commerce platform, which sells car components, accessories and maintenance services to car owners and workshops online. Its funding of around 700 million dollars suggests large venture financing. The available information does not confirm which listing, if any, the company has or how many customers it serves. Operates in the automotive aftermarket in China. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Cava Group is a Washington, DC-based fast-casual Mediterranean restaurant chain known for customizable bowls and pitas with dips, spreads and grilled proteins. It operates over 400 restaurants in the US and also sells packaged dips and spreads in grocery stores. Founded in 2006 by Ted Xenohristos, Brett Schulman and Dimitri Moshovitis, it listed on the NYSE in June 2023 (CAVA), with revenue of over 1 billion dollars. Fast-growing consumer brand skewed to younger urban customers; strong US visibility.

China Southern Airlines is one of China's three largest state-owned airlines, headquartered in Guangzhou, with a fleet of around 900 aircraft serving more than 200 destinations. It flies from hubs in Guangzhou and Beijing Daxing, and is a member of the SkyTeam alliance. Revenue is above 20 billion dollars and it carries more than 100 million passengers a year. Controlled by China Southern Air Holding, a state-owned enterprise, and listed in Shanghai (600029), Hong Kong (1055) and NYSE (ZNH). Strong consumer brand in China and Asia.

Dataiku is an enterprise AI and data science platform that lets analysts, data scientists and engineers build, deploy and govern machine learning and generative AI applications. Founded in Paris in 2013 and now headquartered in New York, it serves large companies in banking, retail, pharma and manufacturing with subscription software. Backed by Tiger Global, Insight, CapitalG, and Snowflake Ventures, it was valued at around 3.7 billion dollars in 2022. B2B software with low consumer awareness; strong among data practitioners.

DHT Holdings is an independent crude oil tanker company that owns and operates a fleet of around 25 very large crude carriers (VLCCs). It charters vessels to oil majors and traders on spot and time-charter markets. Founded in 2005 and headquartered in Oslo, Norway (with Monaco and Singapore operations), it is listed on the NYSE (DHT). It is known for a shareholder-friendly dividend policy. B2B shipping company with no consumer brand visibility.

DIGI RCS & RDS (Digi Communications) is a Romania-based telecommunications group offering cable and satellite television, internet, mobile and fixed telephony, and operating in Romania, Spain, Portugal, Italy, Hungary and Belgium. It is led by founder Zoltan Teszari, headquartered in Bucharest, and listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange (DIGI) and previously on London. It serves millions of subscribers and is a low-price disrupter in several markets. Strong consumer brand in Romania and Hungary; also known for sports TV rights.

Durr Systems (Durr AG) is a German mechanical and plant engineering firm making paint shops, final assembly systems and testing technology for car manufacturers, plus woodworking machines and environmental technology. It is headquartered in Bietigheim-Bissingen in Baden-Wurttemberg, with about 19,000 employees and roughly 4.5 billion euros in revenue. Customers include nearly every large automaker. Listed on the Frankfurt exchange (DUE). B2B equipment maker with industry-level reputation and low consumer awareness.

EcoVadis is a French company that provides business sustainability ratings, assessing suppliers' environmental, social and ethical performance through its collaborative platform. Corporations use it to evaluate supply chains, and suppliers pay to be rated and use its medals. Founded in 2007 in Paris, it has hundreds of thousands of rated companies and large customers such as Johnson & Johnson and Coca-Cola. It raised funding from General Atlantic, Partners Group and CVC, with a valuation of over 1 billion dollars. B2B with low consumer visibility.

Enity Bank Group is a Stockholm-based Nordic banking group, described by Crunchbase as a consortium of mortgage banks focused on financial services and mortgages. Funding of roughly 775 million dollars is shown. The input does not state which banks it combines, who owns it, or its customer numbers, so assume a lender serving retail borrowers in Sweden and neighbouring countries. Mortgage banks of this kind have low consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Flash Express is a Thai logistics company that operates a parcel and express delivery network in Thailand, delivering e-commerce parcels to consumers and small businesses with a large fleet of vans and a network of branches. Founded in 2018 by Komsan Lee and backed by Chinese investors including Alibaba affiliates and Mubadala, it expanded into Malaysia, Laos and the Philippines. Headquartered in Bangkok, with funding of about 780 million dollars. It handles millions of parcels daily. Moderately known as a delivery brand in Thailand.

Genki Forest is a Chinese beverage company launched in 2016, known for sugar-free sparkling water, particularly with flavours, and for tea and milk tea products. Its marketing is internet-driven, with heavy social media and celebrity endorsements, and it is sold through convenience stores and e-commerce. It is headquartered in Beijing and backed by Sequoia China, HillHouse and Tiger Global, valued at about 6 billion dollars in 2021. Strong young-consumer brand in China, with sponsorship of sport and esports events.

Global Fashion Group is an e-commerce group running online fashion and lifestyle platforms in emerging markets, including Dafiti (Latin America), ZALORA (Southeast Asia and Hong Kong), THE ICONIC (Australia and New Zealand) and Lamoda (Russia, divested). Founded in 2011 by Rocket Internet and partners, it is headquartered in Luxembourg with operations in London. It listed on the Frankfurt exchange in 2019 (GFG). The stated London location matches its operating office. Consumer brands with solid regional awareness.

Inceptio Technology is a Chinese autonomous trucking company, founded in 2018, that develops L3 driver assistance and self-driving systems for heavy trucks and sells freight services via its fleet. It is headquartered in Shanghai with an office in Santa Clara, California, and has backers including CATL, Meituan and Hillhouse. Funding of around 680 million dollars is shown. B2B logistics technology; it is not a consumer brand. Its core customers are freight fleets in China.

Indika Energy is an Indonesian integrated energy company with interests in coal mining (Kideco Jaya Agung), energy services, infrastructure and increasingly in electric vehicles and renewable energy. It is listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (INDY), headquartered in Jakarta, and controlled by Agus Lasmono Soetikno and associated holders. It has diversified into new energy businesses including nickel and the Indika EV venture. B2B energy conglomerate with little consumer awareness.

Intrepid Fiber Networks is a US fibre network developer and operator headquartered in Broomfield, Colorado. According to the Crunchbase description, it is a telecommunications company; it builds and operates fibre infrastructure and sells wholesale fibre capacity and broadband services in the US. The funding shown is around 715 million dollars, which suggests private equity or infrastructure financing. The details of its network size and owners are not stated in the input. B2B infrastructure with low brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

KEB Hana Bank is one of South Korea's largest banks, formed from the 2015 merger of Hana Bank and Korea Exchange Bank under Hana Financial Group. It offers retail, corporate and foreign exchange banking, with a strong position in international remittance and foreign currency services and a network of overseas branches in Asia, Europe and the Americas. Headquartered in Seoul, Hana Financial is listed on the Korea Exchange (086790) and the NYSE-listed ADRs were delisted. Well-known Korean banking brand with a record of sports sponsorship, notably football.

Lobito Atlantic Railway is the operator of the Lobito Corridor rail line in Angola, running from the Atlantic port of Lobito east to the border with the Democratic Republic of Congo, with the aim of linking copper and cobalt mines of Congo and Zambia to the sea. It won a 30-year concession in 2022, held by a consortium of Trafigura, Mota-Engil and Vecturis, and received US and European financing as part of a Lobito Corridor initiative. Based in Lobito, Angola. B2B freight operator and mining logistics with no consumer visibility.

ManoMano is a French online marketplace for DIY, home improvement and gardening products, founded in 2013 and headquartered in Paris. It lists several million products from merchants and sells to consumers and professionals in France, Spain, Italy, Germany, the UK and Belgium. Backed by Eurazeo, Bain Capital Ventures, General Atlantic and Aglae, it was valued at roughly 2.6 billion euros in 2021. Revenue came from commissions and advertising. Strong consumer brand awareness in France and Southern Europe, with TV advertising.

MPC Container Ships ASA is an Oslo-listed company that owns and charters feeder container ships (roughly 1,000-3,000 TEU) to liner companies such as Maersk, Hapag-Lloyd and MSC. It was set up in 2018 by the German MPC Munchmeyer Petersen group and is listed on Oslo Bors (MPCC), with a fleet of over 60 vessels. Charters are mostly short- to medium-term, which gave strong earnings during the container market boom. Offices in Oslo and Hamburg. B2B shipping with no consumer brand visibility.

OutSystems is a low-code application development platform that lets enterprises build, deploy and manage web and mobile applications quickly, with AI-assisted development tools. It sells subscriptions to large organisations in financial services, insurance, healthcare, government and retail, with several thousand customers worldwide. Founded in Portugal in 2001 and now headquartered in Boston, it is backed by KKR and Tiger Global (valued at around 9.5 billion dollars in 2021) and has well over 1,000 employees. B2B software with little consumer awareness.

Phoenix Power is the operator of the Sur independent power plant in Oman, a roughly 2,000 MW combined-cycle gas-fired plant at Sur, Ash Sharqiyah, selling electricity to Oman Power and Water Procurement Company under long-term contracts. It is owned by a consortium led by Japan's Sumitomo Corporation with Kansai Electric and Oman-based Phoenix investors. Funding total shown is around 720 million dollars, consistent with project financing. B2B power producer with no consumer brand visibility.

PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur (PT SMI) is an Indonesian state-owned infrastructure financing company, owned by the Ministry of Finance, based in Jakarta. It provides loans, project preparation, advisory and equity investment for infrastructure such as toll roads, power, water, transport and, more recently, the post-pandemic recovery and energy transition platforms. It also manages regional development funding programmes, and has issued bonds in local and foreign markets. Government-owned B2B and government lender, with low consumer brand awareness.

QMC Telecom is a wireless infrastructure operator based in San Juan, Puerto Rico, which owns and operates towers and related communications infrastructure. The input shows a communications infrastructure focus and funding of about 700 million dollars. It leases tower space to wireless carriers in Puerto Rico and possibly neighbouring territories, though customer lists and tower counts are not stated. B2B infrastructure, no consumer visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Razorpay is an Indian fintech company, founded in 2014 in Bengaluru, that provides payment gateway, payroll, business banking (RazorpayX), lending and POS services to businesses. It processes a large share of India's online payments for merchants from startups to large enterprises. It raised funding from Tiger Global, GIC, Sequoia, Lone Pine and others, reaching a valuation of around 7.5 billion dollars in 2021, and moved to redomicile its holding in India. B2B brand that is very well known in India's startup and online merchant circles.

Ren-Gas is a Finnish clean energy company building power-to-gas plants that turn renewable electricity and captured carbon dioxide into synthetic methane and other e-fuels, intended for transport and industry. Headquartered in Espoo, it is a developer with projects in Finland and elsewhere in Europe, and its investors include Finnish institutional backers. Funding shown is around 700 million euros or dollars in project-level financing. B2B energy developer with limited consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Junlebao Dairy (Shijiazhuang Junlebao Dairy) is a Chinese dairy producer from Hebei province, best known for its Junlebao infant formula, liquid milk and yogurt products. It sells through retail stores, supermarkets and e-commerce nationwide. Founded in 1993 and headquartered in Shijiazhuang, it was among the infant formula brands that rebuilt after the 2008 melamine scandal (a Sanlu affiliate in the same city), and it later raised funding from investors including CITIC and Taikang, and was planning a Hong Kong listing. Consumer food brand with solid regional recognition in China.

StockX is a Detroit-based online marketplace for sneakers, streetwear, electronics, collectibles and trading cards, which works like a stock market with live bids and asks and authenticates items in its own centres. It earns a transaction fee and seller fee on each sale and serves millions of buyers and sellers worldwide. Founded in 2015 by Dan Gilbert, Josh Luber and others, it was valued at about 3.8 billion dollars in 2021. It has had legal disputes with Nike. Strong brand with younger sneaker-focused consumers.

Tuhu (Tuhu Car Care, 途虎养车) is a Chinese car maintenance and parts platform operating online-to-offline: customers order tyres, oil, batteries and servicing online and have them fitted at a network of thousands of partner workshops and company-run stores. Headquartered in Shanghai and founded in 2011, it listed in Hong Kong in 2025 (9690). It is backed by Tencent, Sequoia China and other investors, and is a significant name in Chinese automotive aftermarket services. Recognized consumer auto service brand in China.

Unison is a San Francisco-based fintech offering shared-equity home financing, in which it helps buyers with a down payment in exchange for a share of the home's future appreciation, with no monthly payments on that portion. Funding of about 693 million dollars is shown, indicating institutional capital used to fund these investments. Details of ownership and current activity are not stated in the input. Real-estate fintech with limited consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Woolworths Group is Australia's largest retailer, operating Woolworths supermarkets, Metro Food Stores, BIG W discount department stores and Petstock, plus the Woolworths Rewards loyalty scheme, and in New Zealand it runs Countdown, rebranded Woolworths NZ. It has well over 1,000 stores and about 200,000 employees, with revenue near 67 billion Australian dollars. Headquartered in Bella Vista, Sydney, and listed on the ASX (WOW). Dominant mass-market grocery brand in Australia with huge consumer visibility and long-running sponsorship programmes.

Archer Well Company is a global oil services company offering well services, including well integrity, wireline, plug and abandonment, platform drilling and engineering for oil and gas operators on land and offshore. It was formed in 2007 as an offshoot of Seadrill-related interests and is headquartered in Sandnes, Norway, with operations across the North Sea, Americas, Middle East and Asia. It was listed on Oslo Bors (ARCH). B2B energy services provider with no consumer visibility.

Arqiva is a UK communications infrastructure and media services company. It owns and operates the national terrestrial TV and radio broadcast transmission network, thousands of towers and masts, and is a major provider of smart metering communications and satellite and media services. Customers include broadcasters, mobile operators and utilities. It is headquartered near Winchester, Hampshire, and has been owned by a consortium including Macquarie, IFM and Ontario Teachers' pension plan. B2B infrastructure brand with moderate recognition in the UK media sector.

Baibu (Baibu, 百布) is a Chinese B2B online trading platform for textiles and fabrics, connecting garment makers with fabric mills and suppliers, with services such as sourcing, logistics and payment. It is based in Guangzhou, Guangdong, close to the apparel manufacturing base, and has raised funding of around 570 million dollars. Further data about scale or ownership is not available from the input. B2B marketplace with no consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Banco Consorcio is a Chilean financial services group providing banking, insurance, mortgages and asset management to individuals and companies, with a well-known life insurance business (Consorcio Nacional de Seguros) and a bank dating to the late 1990s. It is part of Consorcio Financiero, listed on the Santiago exchange, headquartered in Santiago. Funding around 590 million dollars is shown. Moderately known Chilean financial brand with a middle-market consumer base.

Banco Davivienda is one of Colombia's largest banks, founded in 1972 as a savings and housing corporation and now a full-service bank offering retail, corporate, mortgage, credit card and digital banking, with a regional presence in Panama, Costa Rica, Honduras, El Salvador and Peru, after taking over HSBC and Citibank units. Headquartered in Bogota and controlled by the Sarmiento Angulo group (Grupo Bolivar). Listed on the Colombian exchange (PFDAVVNDA). Very visible Colombian consumer bank brand with a red house logo.

Banco Santander Totta is the Portuguese subsidiary of Spain's Banco Santander, providing retail, corporate and private banking, insurance and asset management through branches across Portugal, after acquiring the Totta & Acores and Banco Chemical-related networks and merging with Banco Popular Portugal. Headquartered in Lisbon, it is one of Portugal's three largest private banks, with about 400 branches and around 5,000 employees. Wholly-owned by Banco Santander, formerly listed on Euronext Lisbon. Strong consumer brand in Portugal, known for sports and cultural sponsorship.

Bianlifeng is a Chinese chain of cashier-free convenience stores, branded Bianlifeng (Convenience Bee), founded in 2016 and headquartered in Beijing. It operates over a thousand 24-hour stores using self-checkout, with fresh food and snacks, mainly in Beijing and cities such as Shanghai and Hangzhou. It is backed by Tiger Global, Hillhouse, Sequoia and others, raising about 650 million dollars. Strong local urban brand in Chinese big cities, popular among young office workers.

Carter's is an American apparel company specialising in baby, toddler and children's clothing, sold under Carter's, OshKosh B'gosh, Skip Hop and Child of Mine (Walmart) brands. It sells through its own stores, wholesale partners such as Target and Walmart, and online, with revenue near 2.9 billion dollars. Founded in 1865 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. Listed on the NYSE (CRI). Highly visible family consumer brand in North America, particularly among parents of infants.

Christian Louboutin is the French luxury fashion house of designer Christian Louboutin, founded in 1991 and famous for women's shoes with red lacquered soles, and now also men's shoes, handbags, beauty and eyewear. It sells through its own boutiques and e-commerce store and selected department stores worldwide. Based in Paris, it is privately held, with Exor (Agnelli family) buying a minority stake in 2021. Revenue is estimated at several hundred million euros. Very strong luxury consumer brand recognition.

Collibra is a data intelligence and governance software company, offering a platform for data catalogues, data quality and privacy compliance used by large enterprises in finance, pharma and government. Founded in 2008 in Brussels, it is now headquartered in New York, with a valuation of 5.25 billion dollars after its 2021 funding round led by ICONIQ, Index Ventures and Tiger Global. B2B software with no consumer visibility.

Gong is a revenue intelligence software company that records and analyses sales calls, meetings and emails with AI to give sales teams insight on deals and coaching. Founded in 2015 in Israel by Amit Bendov and Eilon Reshef, it is headquartered in San Francisco and valued at 7.25 billion dollars in 2021. Customers are B2B sales organisations, with thousands of enterprise accounts. Investors include Coatue, Sequoia, Salesforce Ventures and Thrive. B2B software brand with strong awareness in sales technology but none among consumers.

HeyTea (Xicha) is a Chinese premium tea chain founded in 2012 in Jiangmen, Guangdong, and now based in Shenzhen, popularising cheese tea (cream cheese topping on tea) and fruit teas. It operates thousands of stores across China, with a mobile ordering app and numerous co-branded products with fashion and gaming brands. It is backed by Sequoia China, Tiger Global and Coatue and was reported to be preparing a Hong Kong listing. Very strong young-consumer brand in China, known for collaborations.

Highspot is a sales enablement platform that helps sellers find content, prepare for meetings and coach reps, with AI features, serving enterprise sales organisations. Founded in 2012 in Seattle, Washington, it has raised more than 640 million dollars, with backers including Salesforce Ventures, Tiger Global, Shasta and Bain Capital Ventures. In 2024-2025 it moved into acquisitions, including merging with Seismic-like competitors. B2B software with some visibility in sales technology circles, no consumer awareness.

Kajabi is an all-in-one platform for knowledge entrepreneurs and creators to build, market and sell online courses, memberships, coaching and podcasts, bundling website, email, payments and community tools. Based in Irvine, California, and founded in 2010 by Kenny Rueter and Travis Rosser, it earns monthly subscriptions from tens of thousands of creator businesses. It raised 550 million dollars from Tiger Global and Insight Partners and others. Well known among online creators, little general consumer awareness.

Korea Investment & Securities is a South Korean brokerage and investment bank, part of Korea Investment Holdings. It offers retail brokerage, wealth management, investment banking, trading, asset management and a mobile trading app, and is one of the country's largest securities houses. Headquartered in Seoul, it is part of the Dongwon Group. Moderately well known Korean financial brand; Crunchbase funding is probably recorded for its debt or fundraising.

Kumho Tire is a South Korean tyre manufacturer founded in 1960 and now majority owned by Chinese tyre maker Doublestar (acquired 2018). It produces passenger car, SUV, truck and racing tyres under the Kumho and Marshal brands, sold in over 100 countries, with plants in Korea, China, Vietnam and the US (Macon, Georgia). Kumho Tire USA is based in Atlanta. Revenue is around 3 billion dollars. Consumer brand that has sponsored motorsport, including the WRC and drift series, and football clubs.

Millicom, trading as Tigo, is a telecommunications and cable company with operations in Latin America, including Colombia, Guatemala, Paraguay, Bolivia, Honduras and Panama, offering mobile, cable TV, broadband and mobile financial services. It was founded in Sweden in 1990 as Millicom International Cellular, is registered in Luxembourg and listed on Nasdaq (TIGO) with a US headquarter in Miami. Serving around 45 million mobile customers. Tigo is a high-profile consumer brand in Latin America, a sponsor of football and cycling.

Movile is a Brazilian technology and investment group, parent of iFood, the leading Brazilian food delivery app, and the owner of other apps and holdings such as Sympla (events), Rappi stake interests and Zoop. Founded in 2000 and headquartered in Sao Paulo, it is backed by Naspers/Prosus and Innova Capital. Its main value lies in iFood, which has tens of millions of orders per month. Movile itself is a holding with lower public visibility, while iFood is a household name in Brazil.

Oman Arab Bank is a commercial bank in Oman, headquartered in Ruwi, Muscat, offering retail, corporate and SME banking, personal loans, cards and Islamic banking services through its branch network. It was formed in 1984 and is listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange (OAB), with partner holdings including Omani families and regional institutions. Consumer bank with moderate local brand recognition in Oman. The Crunchbase funding total is probably debt or capital raising.

PKO Bank Hipoteczny is a Polish mortgage bank, a subsidiary of PKO Bank Polski, Poland's largest bank. It issues mortgage covered bonds and provides home loans for consumers via the PKO network, based in Warsaw. It is listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (PKO). Funding is shown in Polish zloty (about 2.2 billion). Its customers are mostly reached through the parent's branches, so it has limited stand-alone brand awareness, although the PKO name is hugely recognised in Poland.

Qantas is Australia's flag carrier and largest airline, founded in 1920, operating Qantas, QantasLink, Jetstar and Qantas Freight, with a fleet of around 300 aircraft and a Frequent Flyer programme with over 14 million members. Headquartered in Mascot, Sydney, and listed on the ASX (QAN), it has about 25,000 employees and revenue near 20 billion Australian dollars. Very high consumer brand visibility in Australia and the Asia-Pacific, with a flying kangaroo logo; long-term sponsor of Australian sport including the Wallabies and cricket.

R.Power Renewables is a Polish developer of renewable energy projects, mostly solar and wind farms, with a pipeline of several gigawatts in Poland, Spain, Italy and other European markets. It sells projects or electricity under power purchase agreements, and also operates its own plants. Headquartered in Warsaw, it was founded in 2015 and is backed by Fortress-linked and Polish private investors. B2B energy developer with limited consumer visibility; Funding shown is about 670 million dollars.

Weilong Foods is a Chinese snack food company headquartered in Luohe, Henan, best known for spicy gluten strips (latiao), under the Weilong brand, as well as konjac products and vegetable snacks. Strong youth snack brand across China; sponsorship rooted in food and consumer entertainment.

Wizz Air is a Hungarian ultra-low-cost airline, founded in 2003 and headquartered in Budapest, with a fleet of roughly 200 Airbus A320 family aircraft flying to more than 190 destinations across Europe, the Middle East and Central Asia, carrying about 60 million passengers a year. Yipin Fresh (Yipin Xianshi) is a Chinese discount fresh food and grocery distributor based in Hefei, Anhui. Al Salam Bank-Bahrain is an Islamic retail and commercial bank headquartered in Manama, offering Sharia-compliant banking, financing, investment and takaful services to individuals and corporates in Bahrain, with a subsidiary in Algeria. Amanecer Puerto Rico is a power project in Puerto Rico, described by Crunchbase as aiming to lower electricity costs and improve reliability. Applied Data Finance (ADF) is a San Diego-based credit and lending technology firm, running the Personify Financial consumer lending brand, providing installment loans and other credit to near-prime consumers through banks and online partners. Athabasca Oil is a Calgary-based Canadian energy company producing heavy oil and light oil, with thermal oil sands assets at Leismer and Hangingstone in the Alberta oil sands and light oil development in the Duvernay. Bandhan Bank is an Indian private-sector bank headquartered in Kolkata, which began as a microfinance institution (Bandhan Financial Services) in 2001 and became a universal bank in 2015. Bank AlBilad is a Saudi Arabian Sharia-compliant commercial bank headquartered in Riyadh, offering retail, private, corporate and treasury banking and remittance, and is known for its digital retail products. Ceres Power is a British fuel cell and electrolyser technology company based in Horsham, West Sussex, that licenses its steel-cell solid oxide technology to partners such as Bosch, Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai and Shell, rather than manufacturing at large scale. B2B clean-tech licensing business with strong industry profile but little public awareness.

Claros Mortgage Trust is a US commercial real estate finance REIT, externally managed by Mack Real Estate Credit Strategies (a unit of Mack Real Estate Group), which originates senior and mezzanine transitional loans on multifamily, office, hotel and mixed-use properties. Cyxtera Technologies was a data centre and colocation operator, spun out of CenturyLink's assets in 2017 and owned by BC Partners, with about 60 facilities worldwide and the Cyxtera Cyber fabric. B2B infrastructure with limited public awareness.

Degreed is a learning experience platform that lets employees aggregate and track learning from many sources, with skills tracking and career development tools for enterprises. Customers include large corporate clients, with millions of learners. B2B software that is little known to consumers.

Doncasters is a UK-based manufacturer of precision-engineered components for aerospace, defence, industrial gas turbine and energy markets, including superalloy castings, forgings, and fabricated parts for jet engines. B2B supplier to engine makers such as Rolls-Royce, Pratt & Whitney and GE, with no consumer awareness.

B2B infrastructure with little consumer awareness.

egg Power is the clean energy investment arm of the telecommunications group, set up to invest in renewable energy projects. Flowserve is a Texas-based manufacturer of flow control equipment, including pumps, valves, seals and related services, for oil and gas, chemical, power generation, water and general industrial customers. General Fusion is a Canadian fusion energy company founded in 2002 by Michel Laberge, developing magnetized target fusion technology that compresses plasma with a liquid metal wall. Global Loan Agency Services (GLAS) is a financial services provider offering loan agency, security trustee, trustee and escrow services to lenders and borrowers in syndicated loan and bond transactions. GOAT Group is a Los Angeles-based online marketplace for sneakers, apparel and accessories, which sells new and pre-owned items from authenticated sellers, and owns Flight Club retail stores. Groupe CCF is a French banking group (formerly Credit Commercial de France) that offered retail banking, corporate and private banking, and was acquired by HSBC in 2000, becoming HSBC France. HashKey Capital is a digital asset investment firm and venture arm of the HashKey Group, a Hong Kong-based crypto financial services business that operates the licensed HashKey Exchange. Infleqtion is a quantum technology company working with neutral atom quantum computing, atomic clocks, quantum sensors and navigation systems, selling to government, defence and commercial customers. B2B and government deep-tech brand with no consumer awareness.

JetZero is a California aerospace startup developing a blended wing body (all-wing) passenger aircraft, the Z4, designed to cut fuel burn by about half versus conventional airliners. Pre-revenue; B2B aviation with low consumer visibility.

Jindal Power is an Indian independent power producer, part of the Jindal group, headquartered in New Delhi. B2B power company without a consumer-facing brand, although the Jindal name is well known in Indian industry.

Kraken Robotics is a Canadian marine technology company based in Mount Pearl, Newfoundland, producing synthetic aperture sonar, subsea batteries, laser scanners and underwater robotics for defence, offshore energy and ocean mapping customers. B2B deep-tech supplier with no consumer brand profile.

Licious is an Indian direct-to-consumer meat and seafood brand, founded in 2015 in Bengaluru, that sells fresh chicken, mutton, fish and ready-to-cook products through an app and cold-chain delivery network in major cities. Well-known urban consumer food brand, with celebrity marketing in India.

Lunar Energy is a US residential energy storage and software company, founded in 2022 by Kunal Girotra (former Tesla Powerwall leader) and Kevin Doran, offering Lunar System home batteries and Gridshare software that aggregates batteries into virtual power plants. Young brand with modest consumer awareness.

Maurel & Prom is a French independent oil and gas company that explores and produces hydrocarbons, mainly in Gabon (Ezanga and other fields), Tanzania, Angola, Nigeria, Italy and Colombia. Mercury Insurance is a US property and casualty insurer, founded in 1961 and headquartered in Brea, California, writing mainly personal auto insurance along with homeowners, renters and commercial policies. Well-known West Coast consumer insurance brand with significant regional advertising.

Metagenomi is a California biotechnology company, based in Emeryville, developing gene editing therapies using novel CRISPR systems discovered from metagenomic sequencing and machine learning. Pre-revenue biotech with funding of roughly 467 million dollars. No consumer visibility.

Moglix is a Singapore- and India-based B2B e-commerce and supply chain platform for industrial products and business supplies, founded in 2015 by Rahul Garg, selling tools, safety equipment, electricals and raw materials to manufacturers and contractors, and also providing financing and sourcing services. Muon Space is a US satellite company, founded in 2021 and based in Mountain View, California, which designs, builds and operates satellite constellations for climate and Earth observation, including its FireSat constellation for early wildfire detection with Earth Fire Alliance. o9 Solutions is a Dallas-based provider of cloud planning software, the o9 Digital Brain platform, for demand planning, supply chain, revenue management and integrated business planning, used by large consumer goods, retail and industrial companies. B2B enterprise software, known in supply chain circles, with no consumer visibility.

OnlyFans is a London-headquartered subscription content platform where creators sell access to photos, videos and live streams directly to fans, mostly adult content creators but also fitness, music and lifestyle. PagerDuty is a San Francisco-based digital operations management platform that alerts engineering teams about incidents, coordinates response and automates workflows, with AI features, used by thousands of companies including large enterprises. B2B developer tool brand with strong recognition among software and IT operations teams, none among general consumers.

Pearson is a British education company based in London, selling digital learning, assessments, qualifications (Edexcel), English language learning (Pearson Test of English, Versant), textbooks and the virtual schools and workforce skills. PLD Space is a Spanish aerospace company based in Elche that develops reusable launch vehicles for small satellites, including the Miura 5 rocket, after its suborbital Miura 1 flight in 2023. B2B launch provider with growing profile in European space, minimal consumer awareness.

Pleo is a Danish fintech company providing company cards, expense management and spend control for small and medium businesses in Europe. B2B fintech with solid brand recognition among European SMEs.

Radiant is a nuclear energy startup based in El Segundo, California, developing the Kaleidos portable microreactor, a high-temperature gas-cooled reactor that is sized to be transported in a container for remote sites, military bases and data centres. Red Cat Holdings is a drone technology company that makes military and commercial drones, such as the Teal Drones Black Widow quadcopter, which was selected for the US Army's Short Range Reconnaissance programme, and FPV Skypersonic and Fat Shark goggles. Renasant Bank is a US regional bank headquartered in Tupelo, Mississippi, with about 190 branches across Mississippi, Tennessee, Alabama, Georgia, Florida and Texas, offering consumer, commercial, mortgage and wealth management services. Well-known community bank in the US South, sponsor of local sports and events.

Ripple Prime is the institutional prime brokerage and credit network unit of Ripple, which provides trading, financing and clearing services for institutional clients across digital assets and traditional markets. B2B institutional brand with strong crypto awareness through Ripple, and Ripple has sponsored sports.

Ruigu (Ruigu, 睿谷) is a Shanghai-based Chinese B2B e-commerce platform focused on the sale of electronics and hardware components, with funding of around 500 million dollars shown. Skyryse is a Los Angeles aerospace company that develops a universal flight automation system, SkyOS, which simplifies and automates aircraft controls for pilots, retrofitted to existing helicopters and aeroplanes.
